title: PowerShell Invoked With An Encoded Command Option
detection_hypothesis: If a caller wants to hide the executed statement, the PowerShell command line will contain an encoded command switch followed by an opaque string.

field_semantics.Image: Absolute path of the executable backing the created process.
field_semantics.CommandLine: Full command line including arguments as supplied to the process.

collection_prerequisites: A process creation source is enabled (Sysmon Event ID 1 or Security Event ID 4688).
Command-line auditing is enabled when Security 4688 is the only available source.
expected_collection_gaps: Security 4688 without command-line auditing provides no CommandLine value.
Short-lived processes may be lost if the agent is restarted during collection.
normalization_assumptions: Image and ParentImage are absolute paths using backslash separators.
CommandLine retains the original argument order and spacing.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines lowercase paths; the lab matcher is case-insensitive by default.
Sysmon and 4688 differ in parent process fidelity and in User field formatting.
retention_considerations: Process creation is high volume; 30 to 90 days of hot retention is typical.
expected_volume: Moderate where configuration management is heavily used.
false_positive_strategy: Benign encoded commands originate from a handful of management agents and always have the same parent process. Tune on ParentImage plus the invoking account, not on the encoded switch.
tuning_guidance: Exclude the management agent parent image on managed endpoints. Do not exclude the encoded command switch, and prefer decoding the command in the pipeline for review.
test_strategy: Positive cases use the long and short forms of the switch with a synthetic placeholder string. Negative cases cover an ordinary command, a file-based script, and a different binary.
unmapped_defensive_objects_reason: No Detection Strategy, Analytic, or Data Component identifier for this technique was present in the pinned ATT&CK extraction used by this lab. Defensive arrays are left empty rather than populated with unverified identifiers. Unmapped techniques: T1027.
author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
